inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 200.33m basic shares at 30-Sep-2026 (Q2 FY27 standalone results; 51,430 ESOP shares allotted in H1) plus ~0.2m dilutive options/RSUs (FY26 AR: diluted weighted average 200.26m vs basic 200.06m). Held FLAT: SBC (~0.04% of revenue) is expensed in the flows; no buybacks, no non-SBC issuance.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 standalone cash flow statement 'Employee stock compensation cost' add-back (Rs 17.64 crore); no net-share-settlement tax line exists (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). India is effectively an SBC-zero market for this name.
inputs.wacc_rationale: INR-built, all-equity (no borrowings). Risk-free ~6.5% (India 10y G-sec); ERP ~7% (India total ERP incl. country premium, Damodaran-style); beta ~0.8 for a debt-free, cash-rich consumer-cyclical leader -> cost of equity ~12.0% = WACC. Terminal growth 5.0% in INR = ~4% inflation + ~1% real (below India nominal GDP because the 100cc commuter core is mature and EV substitution caps real growth). Risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not via a WACC premium; WACC identical across scenarios. The 15% hurdle is INR-denominated, i.e. only ~3pp above WACC (vs ~4-5pp for a USD build) because INR inflation is ~2pp above USD.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: Ind AS 116 EBITDA excludes lease cost; lease liabilities Rs 733.44 crore at 30-Sep-2026 (642.04 non-current + 91.40 current; jumped from 189.56 at Mar-26 on a new ROU lease) are total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; ROU depreciation sits in the D&A/capex paths. Lease cash (~Rs 30 crore/half) is immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: None. Standalone entity, wholly owned; subsidiaries (HMCL Colombia, Netherlands, Americas, HMC MM Auto) and associates (Hero FinCorp 40.45%, Ather Energy ~30%+, Euler Motors 34.12%) are NOT in the flows and enter the equity bridge instead.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing: non-US cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations). Valued on the STANDALONE accounts: consolidated would fold in Hero FinCorp (an NBFC lender) whose borrowings are operating funding, not net debt. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). FY0 = FY2026 (year to 31-Mar-2026); year 1 = FY2027, of which H1 is already reported (revenue Rs 27,686 crore, +27.6% YoY; EBITDA margin 13.3%). OWNER FCF: reported FY26 FCF = OCF 83,149 - capex 10,059 = 73,091; less SBC 176 = 72,914. interest_income is 0 BY CONSTRUCTION, not by omission: under Ind AS the standalone cash flow removes interest, dividend income and MF gains from OCF and shows them in investing, and EBITDA excludes other income, so treasury income (~Rs 1,041 crore FY26) is already outside both reported FCF and every projected flow while the treasury is added in the bridge -- counted once. FY26 FCF is NOT a run-rate base: OCF was flattered by a ~Rs 2,000 crore+ payables-driven working-capital inflow on the post-GST-cut Q3-Q4 volume surge and a 15.7% cash tax rate (vs 25.17% statutory). The component build year-1 owner FCF is ~Rs 4,700 crore (~8.6% of revenue), not ~Rs 7,300 crore; that normalization is deliberate. CAPEX: FY27 guidance Rs 1,500 crore (Q1 and Q2 FY27 presentations) = ~2.7% of revenue for capacity 8.63m -> 9.2m units and GPC 2.0 (Tirupati); historic 1.9-4.8%. WORKING CAPITAL: Hero runs negative working capital (Sep-26 trade payables Rs 9,341 crore vs receivables 3,521 + inventory 2,142 = -Rs 3,678 crore, ~-6.7% of annualized revenue), so growth RELEASES cash: wc_capture positive (5% base). Cash tax 25.168% (new-regime statutory rate used in the AR tax reconciliation) in all years. SBC kept as an explicit 0.04% line; company EBITDA is already after the ESOP charge so that line double-counts ~Rs 20 crore/yr (<0.5% of value) -- left in deliberately as the conservative side. House/street band effectively collapses (SBC-zero market): treat band_position as not meaningful. Known one-offs (FY20 exceptional gain, FY24 Rs 160 crore VRS, FY26 Rs 119 crore labour-code charge) sit below EBITDA and do not touch the margin anchors. Buybacks: none ever (buyback_cash 0); the flat count is a convention the company funds only by issuing almost nothing (~0.05m ESOP shares/yr). Capital allocation leakage risk: Hero recurrently injects cash into associates/ventures (Ather Rs 2,000 crore Q2 FY27, Euler Rs 720 crore FY26, Hero FinCorp capital calls) and has written down past bets (Zero Motorcycles Rs 241 -> 19 crore; HMCL Netherlands impairment). Those outflows are treated as value-neutral transfers into bridge assets, which is generous if future bets underperform; the bear weight carries that.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR (7.3%) is >30% below EPS 5y CAGR (12.1%) and the 3y figures diverge further (8.9% vs 21.8%). Cause is payout, not weak economics: Hero distributes ~65-70% of profit (FY26 DPS Rs 185 = Rs 3,700 crore), so book value structurally lags earnings. The base revenue path (17% FY27 from reported H1, then 9% fading to 5.5%) sits between the equity and revenue CAGRs.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest already outside Ind AS OCF) has CAGRs essentially identical to reported because SBC is ~0.04% of revenue -- no evidence of growth being paid for in stock. The FCF CAGRs are endpoint artefacts and were NOT used: FY23 (Rs 1,985 crore) was a trough and FY26 (Rs 7,291 crore) is inflated by a working-capital release and a 15.7% cash tax rate. FY19 OCF (Rs 979 crore) was also abnormally low. Revenue FY16-FY26 10y CAGR is only 4.3%: FY19-FY23 were flat-to-down (BS-VI cost push, COVID, rural slump), so the 3y figure is a recovery rate, not a trend rate. Volumes FY23 5.33m -> FY26 6.47m (6.7%/yr), ASP Rs 63.4k -> 72.4k (4.5%/yr).

base.growth_rationale: FY27: H1 reported +27.6% (Rs 27,686 crore); H2 assumed ~+8-10% against the post-GST-cut H2 FY26 surge (Rs 25,125 crore) -> ~Rs 54,800 crore, +17%. FY28 onward: industry volume 4-5% + ASP/mix 3-4% (premium, 125cc, PAM growing ~28-30%, exports), less gradual commuter share loss to EV, fading to 5.5% by FY36 to meet the 5% INR terminal.
base.margin_rationale: FY27 13.6%: H1 printed 13.3% (Q2 13.4%) on commodity headwinds; H2 partly recovers with PLI on 100% of VIDA from Dec-26. Mid-cycle 14.0% thereafter = average of FY16-FY26 (11.5%-16.1% range, ten-year mean ~13.9%) and below the FY18 peak; EV mix dilution offsets PAM/premium mix gains.
base.capex_rationale: FY27 guidance Rs 1,500 crore (~2.7%); FY28 2.8% for GPC 2.0 completion (calendar 2027) and EV/premium lines; 2.5% steady state, above D&A (2.0%) because the business is still growing ~5-6% nominal.

scenario_narratives.base: The GST-cut demand pulse fades but does not reverse: FY27 lands ~+17% on the reported H1 and a normal festive H2, then revenue compounds 6-9% on rural recovery, 125cc/premium mix (Glamour X, Xtreme, Harley X440), a parts business growing far faster than vehicles, and exports into Latin America, Africa and Europe. VIDA gains share slowly in a fragmented EV market (TVS/Bajaj lead) and its losses narrow with full PLI eligibility, but EV mix holds group EBITDA at a mid-cycle ~14% rather than the FY18 16% peak. Capex steps up to ~2.7-2.8% for 9.2m units and GPC 2.0, then settles at 2.5%. Negative working capital keeps releasing a little cash as volumes grow.
scenario_narratives.bull: Hero converts its 14,000-touchpoint distribution and commuter-franchise cost lead into EV share: VIDA reaches double-digit, profitable share with PLI and Battery-as-a-Service, scooters move toward 10% share, and Harley/premium plus parts (PAM) lift mix enough to take EBITDA to 15.5% -- above FY26's 14.7% but below the FY18 16.1% peak. Exports become a real second leg (Brazil from H2 FY27, Europe). Revenue grows 10-12% for three years then fades to 6.5%; terminal growth 5.5% reflects a business still riding India's nominal growth. Ather (bridge) is held at market less a 30% discount in every scenario, so EV upside via Ather is NOT added here.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 100cc commuter core -- Hero's highest-share segment -- is the one EV and scooters cannibalise: FY27 growth stalls in H2 as the GST pull-forward unwinds (+11% only because H1 is banked), then 2-4% revenue growth as rural demand and financing tighten and Hero cedes 125cc and EV share to Bajaj, TVS and Honda. Commodity inflation and EV price competition push EBITDA back to the FY22-23 trough band (11.5%) and keep it there, while capex rises to 3.0% to chase EV and scooter capacity that earns little. A new CEO (Jan-2026) mis-steps on the pivot. Terminal growth 4% (inflation only, no real growth). The business still earns a ~6-7% owner-FCF margin -- it is a share-loser, not a going concern question -- and the bear does NOT haircut the treasury.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% house default): the core franchise faces a structural substitution threat (EV and scooters) that rests on an unproven pivot (VIDA has never led EV), the customer base is monsoon- and credit-cyclical, and the CEO is ten months in; the balance sheet removes any solvency tail, which is why bear is not higher. Base 50%: H1 FY27 is already reported, anchoring the guidance year. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs EV share gains, export scale and margin expansion to all go right at once while competitors (TVS, Bajaj) are ahead in EV.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hero is valued as a cash-generative, debt-free cyclical at mid-cycle margins, on standalone accounts, with every non-operating asset added once in the bridge: ~Rs 9,685 crore of current treasury, ~Rs 4,346 crore of long-dated treasury, and the associate stakes (Ather at a 30%-discounted market value, Hero FinCorp and Euler at cost). The operating DCF and the bridge answer different questions -- the bridge is roughly a fifth of the market cap, and over half of it is a single volatile listed EV stock.
key_risks_to_valuation: Ather Energy's share price: the discounted stake (~Rs 14,675 crore) is ~13% of Hero's market cap; a 50% fall in Ather moves Hero's value by ~Rs 370/share.
EV substitution of the 100cc commuter core is the axis between base and bear; margin is the single most sensitive driver (1pp EBITDA ~ Rs 300+/share).
FY26 cash flow is flattered by working capital and low cash tax; anyone anchoring on reported FCF (~Rs 7,300 crore) will see ~50% more value than the component build.
Capital allocation leakage into associates/ventures (Rs 2,700+ crore in 12 months) is treated as value-neutral; past bets (Zero Motorcycles, HMCL Netherlands) were written down.
Hero FinCorp is held at cost; an IPO at a premium to book would add value, a credit-cycle loss and further capital call would subtract it.
The non-current debt-fund figure is a residual estimate (Rs 4,346 crore); a misclassified equity-type item inside it would overstate the bridge.
